owner_intent: ClayVerse should behave like a sealed sandbox/binary-like machine continuum with controlled input/output, complete EntityOS and UnifiedDB inside, direct managed Linux terminal control, and automatic snapshot rollback after EntityOS/internal crashes.
laws: final accepted ClayVerse image contains complete accepted EntityOS substrate
UnifiedDB remains sole canonical persistent state authority
external input crosses explicit ingress and is canonicalized before cognition/execution
LLM output is re-ingested as proposed intent/command before execution
accepted ClayVerse/EntityOS layer directly controls managed Linux PTY/tmux within policy
stdout/stderr/results/effect receipts re-enter the same causal continuum
only explicit attributable egress crosses outward
critical internal crash triggers automatic recovery from last accepted known-good logical machine snapshot
recovery fences stale generation and advances a new runtime generation
ambiguous external effects are not replayed; they become UNKNOWN_AFTER_CRASH unless replay safety is proven
snapshot consistency binds UnifiedDB checkpoint, generations, EntityOS/config/policy hashes, causal queue position and EffectJournal state
stability_rationale: The sealed inner boundary acts as a shock absorber: internal failures are contained and reconstructed without making outside systems the runtime/state authority.
snapshot_note: Logical consistency snapshot is mandatory; CRIU/filesystem/RAM snapshots may later optimize recovery but cannot replace UnifiedDB/EffectJournal consistency rules.
testing_required: crash before/after effect emission and acknowledgement
no blind replay of ambiguous external effects
